summary: GlaS gland-instance annotation plus field-level diagnostic grade transformed into repository semantic fine labels.

annotation_traits: the primary segmentation target is individual gland objects
benign or malignant status is supplied at the image/field level
repository preprocessing transfers field-level context to gland pixels
repository Stroma is the non-gland complement and is not a pure stromal histology annotation
semantic_limitations: Fine tumor subtype IDs are inherited from field metadata and are not independently annotated per gland.
Canonical Stroma denotes non-gland complement and may include lumen, inflammatory tissue, smooth muscle, debris, or other non-gland structures.
Immune, vessel, necrosis, and Other tissue are not independently encoded.

rules.claim: Require the original gland-instance mask digest, field grade, and preprocessing revision; the semantic fine mask alone cannot prove gland identity or independently graded subtypes.
rules.required_observation: Verify all three provenance fields before scene construction and retain instance IDs in the audit artifact.
counterexamples: Calling a fine-12 gland independently expert-labeled as moderately differentiated when the value was propagated from the field.
Editing a semantic mask after losing original gland instance boundaries.
known_limitations: The current scene graph uses semantic components; direct native gland-instance constraints remain to be integrated.

rules.claim: Do not use zero as gland-adjacent stroma or lumen; valid non-gland pixels are represented by the transformed Stroma label, while zero remains protected.
rules.required_observation: Verify exact preservation of zero and choose anchors only between explicit nonzero scene components.
counterexamples: Growing a gland into a zero border region.
Using an internal zero artifact as a gland lumen seed.
expected_morphology: All zero pixels are identical in source and target.
forbidden_morphology: Zero-label seeding, filling, crossing, or relabeling.
known_limitations: Exact transformed zero semantics must be frozen per preprocessing revision.

rules.claim: Treat each annotated gland as an object: a local burden edit must not merge adjacent glands, split one gland, erase its lumen, or create a detached gland island.
rules.required_observation: Trace the complete epithelial contour and lumen in the native instance mask, semantic overlay, and H&E before selecting an anchor.
exceptions: Poorly differentiated fields with no recognizable gland object require explicit observation and a non-gland architecture primitive.
counterexamples: A short deep notch through one side of a gland.
An expansion bridge joining two separate gland instances.
Closing a real lumen because it is a hole in the binary tumor mask.
expected_morphology: A smooth displacement along a sufficiently broad existing gland/non-gland interface.
A recognizable lumen and continuous epithelial boundary remain coherent when present.
forbidden_morphology: Abrupt notches, narrow necks, gland fusion, gland fission, detached epithelial islands, or lumen filling.
known_limitations: Semantic connected components can merge touching instances; native instance topology is the authoritative check.

rules.claim: Interpret transformed Stroma only as non-gland complement; do not assume every pixel is fibrous or desmoplastic stroma.
rules.required_observation: Inspect H&E at the proposed edit band for true tissue support, luminal space, dense mucosa, smooth muscle, inflammatory tissue, debris, or artifact.
counterexamples: Expanding a malignant gland across a large luminal space because the transformed mask calls it Stroma.
Selecting submucosal muscle as a gland-growth reference.
expected_morphology: The chosen source band is visibly compatible with the intended gland boundary change.
forbidden_morphology: Crossing a lumen, muscular wall, debris field, or unrelated dense mucosa under a generic Stroma assumption.
known_limitations: The transformed mask cannot recover non-gland histologic subtypes.

rules.claim: A burden edit must preserve the selected field-derived fine tumor ID and every unrequested gland subtype.
rules.required_observation: Audit changed fine IDs against the primitive transition and recorded patch grade.
exceptions: A separate, explicitly requested differentiation-change primitive.
counterexamples: Turning fine-11 adenomatous gland pixels into fine-12 while only growing tumor.
Using a neighboring field's grade as the target label.
expected_morphology: Fine IDs outside the declared transition remain pixel-identical.
known_limitations: Field-level labels may not capture intrafield heterogeneity.
